sections.html:
West central Iowa's Carroll County had 20,760 residents in 2020, with about half of them, 10,321, in the city of Carroll, the county seat. Manning (1,455), Coon Rapids (1,300, partly in Guthrie County), Glidden (1,151), Arcadia (525) and Breda (500) are the other larger towns. The latest estimate is 20,303, down a little from 20,816 in 2010.

The courthouse at 114 E. 6th Street houses both the treasurer and the assessor, which makes one trip enough for most property tax errands.

Property tax passes through three hands here. The assessor decides what a parcel is worth, the auditor turns local budgets into rates, and the treasurer receives your check.

  • Carroll County Treasurer: ground floor of the courthouse, 114 E. 6th Street, Carroll, IA 51401. Phone 712-792-1200. Takes payments, chases delinquent accounts and runs the June auction.
  • Carroll County Assessor: under the same roof. The county has posted more than one phone number for this office, so try 712-792-9973 or check the county site before you drive over.
  • Board of Review: hears spring protests, with petitions filed through the assessor.
  • Iowa Department of Revenue: sets statewide rules and orders equalization between classes of property.

A full reappraisal is under way and wraps up December 31, 2026. The new numbers start January 1, 2027. The Conference Board approved the project in February 2022, and the county hired Vanguard Appraisals to do the fieldwork.

Appraisers record construction type, interior finish, condition, age and exterior measurements. They do not quote a value at the door. Final value notices go out after January 1, 2027, informal meetings are planned for spring 2027, and bills for fiscal 2028 and 2029 will use them.

Thinking of selling in the coming year? Today's bill still rests on the old valuation, and a buyer looking at a low figure could see a bigger one after the 2027 notices. Expect them to ask. Appraisers rely on Iowa Code section 441.17 for the right to enter property. They knock before exterior work, leave if you ask, and need your permission for interior walk-throughs of new construction.

Carroll County asks for half the tax on September 1 and half on March 1. Interest begins the following month, so October 1 or April 1, and a weekend can nudge the cutoff by a day or two.

Carroll County payment calendar and penalties
Payment eventWhen it applies
First half dueOpens September 1, closes September 30
Second half dueOpens March 1, closes March 31
Late interest1.5% monthly, whole dollars only, with a $1 floor
Mailed paymentsPostmark must come before the delinquent date
Tax sale interest for the buyer2% monthly on the amount sold

A check or cash payment must land with the treasurer by the last business day before the delinquent month, or carry a timely postmark (Iowa Code 445.37). The statement is addressed to whoever holds title, whether or not a lender pays from escrow.

sections.h2: How the June tax sale works
sections.html:
Each year the county auctions unpaid taxes, normally the third Monday of June. Recent sales ran online through GovEase, with bids accepted from 9:00 to 10:30 a.m. People who want to bid sign up ahead of time and pay a $40 registration fee.

Bidding starts at 100 percent and moves down in whole percentages. The lowest percentage wins, and ties go to a random draw. Whoever wins covers the back taxes, interest and a $20 certificate fee. The owner can still redeem by repaying the sale amount with 2 percent added for each month.

  • On an ordinary sale, a 90-day redemption notice may be served once one year and nine months have gone by.
  • Parcels advertised for two years and sold to the public bidder allow the notice after nine months.
  • The redemption amount can include a record search cost of up to $300, plus service and publication costs.
  • Late May is when the Carroll Times Herald prints the delinquent list.

Your petition, in writing, goes to the Board of Review sometime from April 2 through April 30 of the assessment year. Nobody on the board can stretch that window.

Iowa Code 441.37 allows five arguments: unfair comparison with similar property, a figure above legal value, an exemption or classification problem, a clerical error, or fraud. Ask the assessor for a petition form. The Property Assessment Appeal Board also describes each step online.

When the state orders equalization and your class goes up, a short second window opens October 9 to October 31. The only claim allowed then is that the order pushed your value past what Iowa Code 441.21 permits. Rulings can be appealed to the appeal board or to district court within 20 days after adjournment.

SF 2472, signed May 18, 2026, swapped the old homestead credit for an exemption beginning with assessment year 2026. It takes 10 percent off a home's taxable value, never less than $5,500 and never more than $20,000. Bills paid in September 2027 and March 2028 are the first to show it.

Anyone already claiming the credit stays enrolled without refiling. A new buyer files for their own claim.

The city of Carroll runs an urban revitalization area that gives a five year exemption covering the first $75,000 of value added by improvements. Construction has to follow February 25, 2019 in the original area, or November 22, 2021 in the expanded area, and the project must raise assessed value by at least 10 percent.

The city also lists an Infill Housing Incentive of $20,000 per new owner-occupied home while funds last, and a speculative home loan program backed by five local banks. These programs favor new construction, so an older house competes with new homes that carry abatements and incentive money.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes and transfer tax in mind
sections.html:
Most sales credit the buyer with the seller's slice of the current tax at closing, and the settlement statement lays out the split.

A transfer tax of 80 cents per $500 over the first $500 also applies (Iowa Code 428A.1). Each deed travels with a declaration of value signed by a seller or a buyer. The recorder passes it to the assessor, who holds it three years. Who bears the tax is left to the purchase contract.

Water or sewer bills the city has certified to the treasurer turn into a lien ranking alongside ordinary tax, so closing cannot happen until they are paid.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Carroll County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Half on September 1, half on March 1, with interest of 1.5 percent monthly after October 1 and April 1. A weekend can move the cutoff.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Carroll County property tax?
faqs.a: Visit the treasurer's counter at 114 E. 6th Street, Carroll, or phone 712-792-1200. The Iowa Treasurers' site also takes online payments, with a fee for cards and e-checks.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Carroll County assessment?
faqs.a: April 2 to April 30 of the assessment year, filed with the Board of Review. A second window, October 9 to October 31, exists only after a state equalization order raises your value.

faqs.q: Will my Carroll County property tax change after the reappraisal?
faqs.a: Possibly. The reappraisal's values begin January 1, 2027 and drive bills for fiscal 2028 and 2029, with notices arriving after that date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Carroll County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The back tax and interest come out of your proceeds at closing. If the debt was already sold at the June auction, the redemption figure, with its 2 percent monthly charge, is paid as well.
